name: A Servant To Liberty

days.note: Mikey Schaefer's 2016 first ascent topped out pitch 11 almost exactly 11 hrs after starting, climbing through big roofs low on the route then better rock and easier climbing higher up. Descend the standard Beckey-side rappels.
days.title: Long single day

schedule.label: Top out
schedule.detail: ~11 hrs on route, per FA timing

days.objective: Climb A Servant To Liberty (11 pitches)

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day, roughly 11-12 hrs car-to-car including approach and descent.

pitch_detail.notes: Shared start with Freedom or Death: face and crack climbing up a slab to a bolted belay. Locate the correct start among the East Face cluster of routes, not Liberty Crack or Thin Red Line.
Follow bolts up and slightly left/right on sustained face climbing, per the shared Freedom or Death line.
Last pitch shared with Freedom or Death; from here A Servant to Liberty breaks right to join Thin Red Line just below its 3rd-pitch anchor rather than continuing up Freedom or Death.
Starts up easy terrain to a right-leaning overlap with tricky liebacks and smeary feet, the first of the route's new East Face pitches.
Traverses left to flake laybacks protected by two small cams, then stems over a roof and steps right around an arete to the anchor.
Climbs a shallow corner then steps right around a rounded arete on classic golden-granite edges, with a big move back left to a hand rail.
A 165-ft bolted mega-slab with 14 bolts and four cruxy sequences; a 0.75 cam is needed after the second bolt for extra protection.
The route's crux slab pitch: technical, thin edges ('razor blades') and funky foot moves on deteriorating rock that eases to 5.10- near the top. Mikey Schaefer's crux lead of the free route.
Varied, unexpectedly fun 5.10 climbing on decent rock; a #3 cam protects a left-facing corner and small cams cover the final arete traverse.
Short crack past loose blocks; a single bolt lets you avoid a 'kitty litter' loose block on an exposed traverse.
Low-angle left-facing corner with finger cracks protected by nuts, wandering to low-angle terrain and a fixed nut anchor above the trees.

descent_text: A Servant to Liberty (earlier known as 'A Slave to Liberty') climbs the first three pitches of Freedom or Death (5.10, 5.11, 5.11), then steps right onto Thin Red Line just below its third-pitch anchor and continues up eight new pitches of its own. From the top, either scramble to the summit roped and take the standard Liberty Bell descent, or rappel with two ropes; the rappel line given here is Thin Red Line's exit: rappel with two ropes off M&M Ledge (fixed pin/wire anchor), then move climber's-left to bolted anchors for four double-rope rappels back to the base — five rappels total, all on bolted stations.
